titulo: The imperative: Affirmative imperative: tú and usted

aula.objetivo: Give instructions, ask for things, and invite people with the affirmative imperative of «tú», «usted», «vosotros», and «ustedes», learn the eight irregular «tú» forms (ven, di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten), form the negative imperative with «no» + subjunctive, and place pronouns correctly.

blocos.titulo: The affirmative imperative of tú and usted
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the imperative is used to give an instruction, ask for something, invite, or give advice: «Mira», «Escucha», «Pasa». STEP 2: for «tú», the affirmative form is the same as the «él, ella» present-tense form. «Habla» (from hablar), «come» (from comer), «escribe» (from escribir). English's whole imperative, by contrast, is just the bare infinitive with no subject at all — "Look," "Listen," "Wait" — the same single form whether you're talking to one person, several people, a friend, or a stranger. Spanish's split between «tú» and «usted» forms, and the eight irregular «tú» forms coming up next, have no counterpart in English's one-size-fits-all imperative. STEP 3: verbs that change the stem vowel in the present do the same in the imperative: «cierra» (from cerrar), «vuelve» (from volver), «pide» (from pedir), «sigue» (from seguir). STEP 4: eight verbs have an irregular «tú» imperative, and you just have to memorize them: venir → «ven», decir → «di», hacer → «haz», ir → «ve», poner → «pon», salir → «sal», ser → «sé», tener → «ten». STEP 5: for «usted», you don't use the present-tense form; you use the present subjunctive. As a shortcut, just switch the ending's vowel. -ar verbs end in -e instead: «hable», «mire», «espere». -er and -ir verbs end in -a instead: «coma», «escriba», «abra». STEP 6: the «usted» irregulars follow the «yo» present: «venga», «diga», «haga», «vaya», «ponga», «salga», «sea», «tenga». STEP 7: for «ustedes» (more than one person), add «-n»: «hablen», «coman», «escriban». STEP 8: pronouns go after the verb and attach to it: «Escúchame», «Dime», «Siéntate». When you attach the pronoun, the written accent keeps the stress where it was: «escucha → escúchame», «cierra → ciérrala». STEP 9: the imperative only needs «por favor» to sound polite: «Pasa, por favor», «Espere un momento, por favor».
blocos.comparacao: Pronoun attachment is the other piece with no English parallel: English "listen to me" or "sit down" never attaches a pronoun onto the verb itself or shifts its stress — the pronoun is just a separate word that comes after, same as everywhere else in English. Spanish gluing «me» onto «escucha» to make «escúchame», with an added accent mark to keep the stress in place, is a mechanic you'll have to build from scratch.

exemplos.pt: Come in, please, and sit down.

erros.motivo: «Viene» is the present of «él»; the «tú» imperative of «venir» is «ven».

blocos.enunciado: Give a friend five instructions with «tú»: «Ven… Pon… Haz… Ten… Escucha…» Then repeat two of them with «usted».
Say from memory the present of «hablar», «comer», and «escribir», from «yo» to «ellos». Then say two sentences with the future of «tener» and of «hacer».
